subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and what field name, timestamp format, and propagation boundary should be canonical?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing public field semantics and whether this belongs in prompt metadata, trusted metadata, diagnostics, or multiple surfaces is a maintainer product/API decision.

options.title: Define Generic Receive-Time Contract
options.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that keep source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp distinct.

options.title: Keep Timing Internal
options.body: Expose receive-to-dispatch timing through logs or diagnostics instead of agent-visible prompt metadata.

options.title: Defer To Channels
options.body: Let individual plugins add timing where needed, accepting less consistent cross-channel latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Define Generic Receive-Time Contract
recommendation.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that keep source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp distinct.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to adjacent message metadata and API-contract history represented in likelyOwners.
